author: Independent education critic subagent (claude-opus-5-5); did not author or correct the reviewed artifacts

findings.claim: The Activity 3 correction introduced an objective-to-check wording mismatch. Objective o3 (HTML line 369 and topic.json) still says 'choose the collector that produces the intended per-key total', but Activity 3 now asks for each customer's longest ticket and marks the summing merge (Integer::sum) as wrong. A learner who reads the objective first is primed toward the distractor.
findings.recommendation: Reword o3 identically in topic.json, the HTML objectives list and the generated artifact.md, for example: 'Diagnose a stream collection that fails on a repeated key, and choose the merge rule that produces the intended per-key result'.

items.note: Activity 2 now teaches the three-argument groupingBy before the code: its middle argument is a constructor reference, linked to ArrayList::new from method references, that chooses the map type. module.json and coverage plan section 2 now state this small API extension honestly instead of 'no new syllabus'.

The cheat sheet now uses generic forms (history/line/seen, keyFunction/mapFactory/downstreamCollector, keyMapper/valueMapper/mergeFunction, result.map(function).orElse(fallback)). No option text, Ticket:: identifier or keyed result appears outside its fieldset. Recap bullets state the general rules without naming any option's structures.

Activity 3 now has two nested hints. Hint 1 asks for the repeated key, its two values and which one the intended result keeps. Hint 2 explains what a merge function receives and returns and asks the learner to compute each option. Neither hint lists option outcomes.

The hints now escalate on one chain. Activity 1: hint 1 names what comes out or prints first for each need and the lookup frequency; hint 2 points to method ends, contains cost and map iteration order, without the old contrast wording. Activity 2: hint 1 asks which argument sets key order and which sets in-list order; hint 2 deepens that and adds the Optional chain.

Both activities now pose decisions the topic checks did not. Activity 1 adds a lookup-cost trap (thousands waiting, frequent id checks): ArrayDeque.contains is linear, as taught in big-o-basics sources, and the fix is a companion HashSet. Activity 3 now asks for the longest ticket per customer, so the learner must derive the merge function (Integer::max) rather than recognise Integer::sum, which is now a distractor.

topic.json still records artifacts.md status 'present', but the learner directory still contains only artifact.html. This stays open until the deterministic exporter generates artifact.md from the final HTML bytes.

The counting() option was removed. The new option A (Integer::sum) compiles against Map<String, Integer>, and its feedback (Ana would get 50, a total rather than her longest ticket) is accurate. The static alternative matches.

o1 now reads 'Choose the stack, queue, set and map implementations whose ordering and cost guarantees fit a described feature' in both topic.json and the HTML objectives list. That matches the choice-only check, and the success criterion no longer asks for an unobserved justification.

The good fit now describes real scale and purpose (in-memory working state of one running app where an order rule or frequent lookup is part of the feature) without mapping needs to guarantees. The decision and the database boundary are kept.
